behaviors.behavior: Attach bit width and block size metadata, named specialization hints, to each transformed TeSA to help codegen.
behaviors.precondition: A TeSA has been transformed by the execution-plan transformation pass.

evidence.quote: each transformed TeSA is attached with the information about the bit width and block size, named as specialization hints

behaviors.behavior: Pass the specialization hints to the second compilation pass.
behaviors.precondition: Specialization hints have been attached to transformed TeSAs.

evidence.quote: The hints will be passed to the second pass, elaborated next.

behaviors.behavior: Use the bit-width field of a specialization hint to suggest whether to leverage a specific hardware instruction (e.g., DP4A) for the operator.
behaviors.precondition: A hint carrying a bit width is consumed by the second compilation pass.

evidence.quote: the bit-width of an operator suggests whether to leverage a speciﬁc hardware instruction (e.g., DP4A)

behaviors.behavior: Align the operator's loop tiling with the block size from the specialization hint to enable effective dead code elimination (DCE).
behaviors.precondition: A hint carrying a block size is consumed by the second compilation pass.

evidence.quote: the loop tiling of the operator should be aligned with the block size for effective dead code elimination (DCE)

behaviors.behavior: When a specialization hint specifies a block size equal to the tensor's shape (one block covering the whole tensor), use existing general sparse kernels (e.g., cuSPARSE, taco) or a dense kernel if it performs better.
behaviors.precondition: The transformation plan yields a single block covering the entire tensor.
search_terms: block size equal to tensor shape

evidence.quote: A specialization hint could also specify the block size equal to the tensor’s shape (i.e., one block covers the whole tensor).
SparTA can directly use the existing state-of-the-art general sparse kernel implementation (e.g., cuSPARSE [3], taco [53]) or even use the dense kernel implementation if it perform better.

behaviors.behavior: Specialize the same operator code differently according to different transformation plans and their hints (e.g., a smaller block size yields a smaller loop-body Matmul and more DCEs).
behaviors.precondition: The transformation plan (and thus the hints) differs between compilations.

evidence.quote: Given a different transformation plan (and the speciﬁcation hints), the code can be specialized differently.
The hint in Figure 7(c) show a smaller block size. In this case, the loop body is a smaller Matmul (i.e., [2,1]x[1,1]), which enables more DCEs.

behaviors.behavior: Attach a separate bit-width and block-size pair to each operand TeSA participating in an operator (e.g., T and W each annotated separately).
behaviors.precondition: Multiple TeSAs participate in an operator.

evidence.quote: Specialization hints: T: {Bit: 32, Block: 2x2}, W: {Bit: 32, Block: 2x2}
